name: model
character: Peripheral auditory model used by the QA gate: middle-ear weighting, an ERB-spaced cascade of asymmetric resonators, a block-rate compressive gain with spread across neighbouring channels, hair-cell rectification and low-pass, and two-time-constant divisive adaptation. CARFAC-inspired; not a physiological simulation.
sources: Glasberg & Moore 1990: ERB scale for channel spacing (scripts/auditory.py)

Lyon et al., CARFAC v2 (arXiv 2404.17490): cascade of asymmetric resonators with a fast-acting compressive gain; here the serial cascade is kept but the gain control is feed-forward at block rate (knowledgebase/sound-design/virtual-ears.md)
Terhardt absolute threshold (scripts/auditory.py) inverted for the middle-ear weighting, clipped to min_db..max_db; the clip is a starting value

car.zeta, zero_ratio, agc.*, ihc.*, adapt.*, nap.*: starting values chosen so a tone's channel response is about one ERB wide (tests/test_ear_model.py measures it); none is fitted to physiological data
adapt.tau_fast_ms 10 and tau_slow_ms 60 are starting values; the depletion index is a fatigue proxy, not a measured neural quantity
summary.mod_band_hz 30-150 Hz: roughness modulation range around its 70 Hz maximum (knowledgebase/sound-design/roughness.md); pitch_hz 50-700 because the NAP is decimated to 2240 Hz
summary.iacc_band_hz 500-880 Hz: the 880 Hz NAP anti-alias limit leaves this part of the 500-2000 Hz band the room measures use (imm.iacc_early); a starting value
